Senior Manager, Corporate Development About the Role At Klaviyo, we believe in the power of technology to help businesses build smarter, more personalized relationships with their customers. As we continue to expand our platform, product capabilities, and global reach, Corporate Development plays an increasingly important role in accelerating our long-term strategy. We are looking for a Senior Manager, Corporate Development to help shape and execute Klaviyo's inorganic growth strategy, spanning acquisitions, strategic investments, partnerships, and other opportunities that accelerate our product and business ambitions. Reporting to the Head of Corporate Development, you will serve as a strategic partner to senior leadership while independently driving complex, high-impact initiatives from initial thesis development through execution and integration. This is a highly visible, hands-on role with significant autonomy, requiring a unique combination of strategic judgment, financial sophistication, commercial acumen, and the ability to navigate complex transactions across multiple stakeholders. As Klaviyo's platform and ambitions continue to evolve, you will play a critical role in expanding our ability to identify, evaluate, and execute transformative opportunities. Success requires someone who can operate as both a strategic thinker and an exceptional executor, translating market insights into actionable opportunities and driving transactions forward with speed, precision, and sound judgment. How You Will Make a Difference Own end-to-end transaction execution: Independently lead acquisitions, strategic investments, and other inorganic initiatives from opportunity identification and initial evaluation through valuation, diligence, negotiation, internal approvals, closing, and integration planning. Shape Klaviyo's inorganic growth strategy: Partner with the Head of Corporate Development and executive leadership to identify strategic priorities, assess build/partner/buy opportunities, and develop investment theses aligned with Klaviyo's long-term product and business objectives. Drive sophisticated financial and strategic analysis: Build and evaluate complex financial models, transaction structures, valuations, business cases, and synergy analyses to inform investment decisions and capital allocation. Expand deal pipeline and execution capacity: Proactively source, prioritize, and advance multiple opportunities simultaneously, bringing the ownership and operational rigor needed to increase the organization's transaction throughput. Influence executive-level decisions: Develop clear, compelling investment recommendations and present complex strategic, financial, and commercial considerations to senior executives and key decision-makers. Lead cross-functional deal teams: Coordinate Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal, Security, and other stakeholders through complex diligence and transaction processes, ensuring alignment, accountability, and timely execution. Build relationships across the technology ecosystem: Develop and maintain a strong network of founders, investors, advisors, and industry leaders to identify emerging opportunities and strengthen Klaviyo's market presence. Evaluate emerging technologies and markets: Assess evolving industry dynamics, competitive landscapes, AI-driven innovation, and adjacent product opportunities to identify areas where inorganic growth can accelerate Klaviyo's strategy. Navigate complex deal structures: Evaluate and negotiate transaction economics, governance, strategic rights, and commercial considerations across acquisitions, minority investments, and strategic partnerships. Drive post-transaction value creation: Partner with functional leaders to define integration priorities, establish success metrics, and ensure transactions deliver against their strategic and financial objectives. Who You Are 8+ years of relevant experience across Corporate Development, investment banking, private equity, strategic finance, or related transaction-focused roles, including meaningful experience independently leading complex transactions. Demonstrated track record executing acquisitions, strategic investments, joint ventures, or other sophisticated strategic transactions, ideally within technology, software, fintech, or high-growth businesses. Exceptional financial modeling, valuation, and analytical capabilities, with experience evaluating complex business models, transaction structures, and long-term strategic and financial implications. Strong commercial and strategic judgment, with the ability to evaluate opportunities beyond financial returns and understand their implications for product strategy, competitive positioning, and long-term enterprise value. Proven ability to operate with significant autonomy, independently manage competing priorities, and drive multiple complex workstreams from ambiguity to execution. Experience partnering with senior executives and cross-functional leaders, translating complex analysis into concise, actionable recommendations that influence high-stakes decisions. Deep understanding of M&A processes, including strategic evaluation, due diligence, transaction structuring, negotiation, internal governance, and integration planning. Strong relationship-building and negotiation skills, with the ability to engage effectively with founders, investors, external advisors, and senior business leaders. An entrepreneurial, hands-on mindset with a willingness to move seamlessly between high-level strategic thinking and detailed transaction execution. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to develop executive-ready investment materials and clearly articulate complex business decisions. High intellectual curiosity and a strong interest in technology, AI, commerce, and the evolving software ecosystem. Nice to Have Experience executing transactions within a large-scale technology company, high-growth SaaS business, or similarly complex corporate environment. Exposure to international transactions, cross-border investments, or global market expansion. Experience evaluating emerging technologies, AI-enabled businesses, fintech, or adjacent software platforms. MBA or other relevant advanced degree. Experience building or improving Corporate Development processes, transaction frameworks, or analytical infrastructure within a lean, high-performing team. Our best Onboarding Specialists are customer-obsessed, technically curious, and strong project leaders. About the role As Senior Onboarding Specialist, APAC, you'll be the first point of contact for new Klaviyo customers in the region. You'll guide them through their first 30 to 90 days, from sale to a successful go-live, and help them launch the first customer experiences that drive revenue. You'll join as a founding member of our Singapore team, so this role is both hands-on and foundational. Alongside owning a portfolio of onboardings, you'll help shape how Klaviyo onboards customers across APAC: what great looks like, which processes scale, and where the product and onboarding experience need to improve for this market. Our customers vary widely in size, maturity, and technical setup. This role suits someone who enjoys solving unique problems creatively, thrives in challenging situations, and can move easily between technical troubleshooting and strategic marketing advice. How you'll make an impact Own new customer relationships from sale through successful go-live, acting as their trusted guide and advocate throughout onboarding. Lead the implementation phase for each customer, including scope definition, project plans, resourcing, and timelines. Give proactive, strategic advice on Klaviyo best practices so customers hit their initial business goals and build their first campaigns and flows with confidence. Support customers on technical and non-technical questions, including integrations, data setup, marketing strategy, and wider ecommerce configuration. Explain complex concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical users across a wide range of technologies and platforms. Diagnose software issues, resolve customer concerns through established processes, and escalate appropriately when needed. Review customer dashboards proactively, address open issues early, and keep messaging consistent across every touchpoint. Monitor onboarding health, including time to first KAV, across your portfolio and act as a point of escalation when customers are at risk. Set priorities and build technical health plans for open problems so issues are resolved quickly. Run onboarding post-mortems, identify what worked and what didn't, and turn lessons learned into documented best practices. Document troubleshooting and resolution steps to build a shared knowledge base for the growing APAC team. Act as a product expert and bring customer insights to Product and Engineering to improve integrations, setup, UI, and anything else slowing customers down. Surface, coordinate, and drive new ideas to improve onboarding processes as a founding member of the Singapore team. Contribute to a team culture of collaboration, customer empathy, equality, and inclusion. What success looks like New customers reach go-live on time and achieve their first KAV quickly, with strong early engagement on the platform. Customers finish onboarding with a clear strategy, working integrations, and live campaigns and flows that drive revenue. High customer satisfaction and confidence at the end of onboarding, with smooth handoffs to Customer Success. Issues are spotted early, escalated appropriately, and resolved efficiently, with few surprises for customers or internal teams. A growing library of documented best practices, playbooks, and troubleshooting guides tailored to APAC customers. Measurable improvements in onboarding processes and time to value, driven by your post-mortems and feedback. Product and Engineering see you as a credible source of customer insight that shapes real improvements. Customers and internal stakeholders view you as a trusted, proactive operator who can manage complex implementations without heavy manager involvement. Who you are 4+ years of customer onboarding, implementation, or related customer-facing SaaS experience, with a track record of building relationships with multiple stakeholders on an account. Strong project manager with excellent organization skills and experience running several implementations at once. Clear, thoughtful communicator across phone, video, and email, able to adapt to technical and non-technical audiences. Experience helping end users reach key business goals with software. A track record of creative problem-solving for customers. Experience in marketing or advising customers on marketing strategy is a plus. Experience with email marketing and ecommerce platforms is a plus. Foundational knowledge of APIs is advantageous. Comfortable managing customer relationships in Salesforce or a similar CRM, and proficient with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and Google Sheets. AI fluent and comfortable using AI responsibly to improve productivity, sharpen thinking, and model modern ways of working. Curious, eager to learn, and able to adapt in a fast-changing environment. Collaborative by nature, thriving in cross-functional teams. Proactive, accountable, and solutions-oriented; you own outcomes, raise issues early, and improve how work gets done. Fluency in Business Mandarin is required given the customer base across the region. Full authorisation to work in Singapore without restrictions is required. Why this role is compelling APAC is a high-growth region for Klaviyo, and onboarding is where every long-term customer relationship begins. As a founding member of our Singapore team, you'll directly shape how customers across the region experience Klaviyo from day one, build the playbooks others will follow, and have a visible impact on customer growth and retention. If you're excited by helping businesses grow, solving hard customer problems, and building a team from the ground up, we'd love to hear from you. Hands-on experience designing and building AI-powered marketing capabilities, from generative AI use cases to predictive scoring and intent-based automation, that solve real marketing problems. Deep experience architecting HubSpot, Salesforce, and in-house systems at scale, including lead scoring, lifecycle automation, customer journey and personalization, campaign/opportunity data models, and cross-system data association. Strong understanding of marketing budgeting, planning cycles, and ROI measurement — able to connect spend data directly to performance outcomes through architectural decisions. Experience building scalable integrations — using APIs and middleware — across marketing systems (e.g., HubSpot, Salesforce, NetSuite, Coupa). A proven track record contributing to vendor evaluation and platform implementation for enterprise organizations. A natural cross-functional partner — able to sit with cross-functional teams, translate their requirements into system architecture, and be the technical advisor they trust. That shift has made Enterprise our fastest growing segment, with our biggest customers spending well over seven figures a year and, this year, the largest deal in company history. As a Large Enterprise Sales Manager, you'll lead 6 to 8 Account Executives who win new logos and grow our existing customers in the Western U.S. You'll bring out the best in each of them and turn those wins into a repeatable motion. Every deal your team lands is a household name the rest of the market notices. We're looking for a leader who has built enterprise teams before and still loves being in the deal. In your first 90 days, you'll know the book and the top opportunities well enough to help in any of them. Twelve months in, you'll have delivered the year and grown average contract size through multi-product attachment. What you'll do Own the number and the forecast Deliver team bookings against quarterly and annual targets. Call a commit the company can rely on, built from rigorous inspection. Keep the pipeline full Protect the coverage your team needs to hit its numbers. Show AEs how to create territory plans, tier accounts, and map a buying group for every priority account. Raise the standard of AE-led [prospecting / expansion] and what it produces. Win the big deals Sharpen your AEs' discovery, qualification, executive engagement, value cases, and negotiation. Step in yourself where it matters most. Grow the team Hire continuously and get new AEs productive quickly. Run weekly 1:1s that invest in each seller's skills and career. Weave AI into how the team operates. Rally cross-functional partners Work with leaders across Klaviyo so your team never walks into a big meeting alone and has the support it needs. Carry field insight to Product and Enablement. Diagnose what's holding the team back, fix what you can, and escalate the rest early. What you bring 4+ years leading quota-carrying enterprise AEs in B2B SaaS Plus 8+ years of enterprise selling with a record of personal overachievement. Proven ability to teach MEDDPICC or an equivalent methodology. A history of recruiting and developing enterprise sellers who self-source pipeline and hit targets consistently. A track record of building strong tool habits across a team, with Salesforce, Gong, Clari, and AI part of the everyday workflow. Credibility with C-suite executives. Experience leading teams that sell more than one product into the same account. Nice to have: MarTech or ecommerce experience, ideally competing against Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe, or Braze. When we talk, be ready to walk us through a team you moved and a deal you personally changed. We'll go deep on both. We have expanded beyond retail into hospitality, media, healthcare, and business services. You will go after some of the largest brands in the world, including Fortune 500 and Global 2000 companies, prospecting your way in and taking full responsibility for your pipeline target. We partner across the organization, including Sales, Marketing, Engineering & Product, and Customer Service & Success to solve real operational problems with practical, well-designed software. Our work spans internal applications, 3rd party integrations, interactive dashboards, CMS integrations, and robust AI systems and agents that automate repetitive tasks, surface the right information at the right time, and help teams make better decisions. We operate in tight feedback loops with our internal customers, shipping quickly, learning fast, and seeing the impact of our work immediately in how deals move faster, tickets resolve sooner, and launches go more smoothly. As an Amplify EM, you will own klaviyo.com, Klaviyo Academy and the Help Center, along with the systems behind them: our Sanity CMS, the localization pipeline that publishes the site in multiple languages, personalization, and the tooling Marketing uses to produce campaign assets. We are replacing manual content and translation work with AI agents, from agentic translation scored against Smartling's own quality scale, to brief and bill-of-materials generation for campaigns, to automated asset creation in Figma. This role is for builders and leaders who enjoy turning real-world pain points into reliable, scalable solutions. The work is highly visible and deeply impactful, shaping how thousands of Klaviyos get their work done every day through fast iteration, high ownership, and clear outcomes. How You’ll Make an Impact: The Amplify team builds the internal platforms, automation, and AI-driven systems that power how Klaviyos work every day. As an Engineering Manager, you will: Lead the Amplify Marketing and Content Platform engineering teams and set the technical vision for klaviyo.com, Klaviyo Academy, the Help Center, and the content systems behind them. Set and drive the roadmap for moving Marketing's content generation, translation, and asset production onto AI agents. You'll agree on quality bars with stakeholders, decide where a human stays in the loop, and measure each automation by the time and cost it removes. Work side by side with Marketing, Brand, and Localization to map how content actually gets made today, and proactively replace the manual steps with AI agents, from copy and translations to campaign briefs and design assets. Balance technical leadership and people leadership, setting direction, modeling best practices, and enabling teams to deliver efficiently. Partner closely with engineers, product managers, designers, and leaders across Marketing, Brand, Growth, and Localization to turn their biggest bottlenecks into scalable, high-quality software. Own the reliability, performance, and security of klaviyo.com, including on-call, incident response. Foster a culture of innovation, systems thinking, technical excellence, and an AI-first mindset. Build the quality systems that let agents take over human steps safely, including evaluations, observability, and review gates, so Marketing can trust what ships. You and your teams build with agentic coding tools such as Claude Code or Cursor, and you set the standards for how they use them. You have shipped LLM-powered agents or workflows to production that replaced real manual work, with measured outcomes such as hours saved or cost, and you know what makes them reliable: tool use and MCP integrations, multi-step orchestration, human-in-the-loop review, and graceful fallback when the model is wrong. You treat quality as an engineering problem. You have led engineering for a high-traffic marketing website built on a modern front end such as TypeScript and React, owning its performance, SEO, conversion paths, analytics and tagging, and its reliability during launches. You have partnered directly with Marketing, Brand, Growth and Localization teams, and you understand how campaign and content production actually works: briefs, creative review, approvals, launch calendars and last-minute changes. You are a people-first leader and coach, experienced in hiring, onboarding, mentoring, and developing engineers through constructive feedback and growth opportunities, while fostering a healthy, collaborative team culture. You like to question convention and thrive in small, autonomous teams that serve internal customers, ship early and often, and measure success by outcomes such as faster launches, lower cost per asset, and more localized content shipped. You are passionate about building software effectively and for the long term, balancing technical quality, velocity, and business impact. BA or BS Degree in Computer Science, related field, or equivalent experience. Nice to Have: Hands-on experience with internationalization and localization at scale, especially AI-driven translation with tools such as Smartling. Experience using and integrating with headless CMSs like Sanity or Contentful. Experience with experimentation, A/B testing, and personalization platforms such as Optimizely, AB Tasty, or Adobe Target. Experience with Astro, Cloudflare Workers, Figma automation, digital asset management tools such as Bynder, or HubSpot. Klaviyo’s platform is primarily built with Python and React and runs on AWS. Our product doesn't wait on multi-year plans; it evolves in weekly sprints. A business moving at this speed needs an ecosystem that keeps up, and our partners are central to how we grow. Program Partners are a vital part of that story. So we design for self-service first, then wrap it in a local community and a network of peers, so every partner still feels a human connectio n . A partner who doesn't feel valued can't make their full impact. At Klaviyo, we serve our partners through two experiences. Managed partners have graduated to a dedicated, high-touch Partner Account Manager by meeting our tier requirements and graduation thresholds. Program Partners are building their Klaviyo practice, from newly onboarded agencies and boutique specialists to established firms who work with Klaviyo on select projects and referrals. Every Program Partner gets an always-on experience of digital enablement, workshops, office hours, community, and joint go-to-market opportunities, with a clear path to a named Partner Account Manager as their Klaviyo business grows. Our best Partner Managers are commercial, partner-first, and highly collaborative. They know how to turn strong relationships into measurable business outcomes through joint go-to-market planning, co-sell execution, and partner enablement. In this role, you'll bring that approach to every Program Partner at scale. About the role This role primarily supports our Commercial segment, which serves small to medium brands with under $30M in company revenue. As a Partner Account Manager, Program Partners, you will own our Program Partners across the segment: the hundreds of partners who have not yet graduated to managed status. Program Partners are not a consolation prize. They drive new logos and Commercial coverage that other partners won't pursue, and we activate them through self-service portals, on-demand enablement, AI, and community. You'll build a one-to-many growth model that combines partner lifecycle marketing, enablement, community, commercial activation, data, and automation. Your mission: help more partners build and grow a thriving Klaviyo practice, more frequently, so their business and their clients' results grow alongside measurable revenue growth with Klaviyo. You will turn that untapped potential into a reliable, repeatable source of partner-sourced revenue. Our motto is that no partner is left behind, and our north star is that we have no inactive partners. The Klaviyo partner program should be a valuable asset and community for every partner, helping their business, and in turn their clients, grow. Success is measured by partner-sourced pipeline and closed-won attached revenue. We also track the health of the Program Partner book of business through reach (how many partners are active), frequency (how often they source or attach deals), and yield (the value of each deal). Leading indicators such as certification progress, community engagement, portal adoption, and enablement cohort participation show us where to focus next. How you'll make an impact Drive activation and commercial growth Increase the number of partners generating qualified opportunities and repeatable partner-sourced revenue. Build growth plays that help partners move from onboarding to first registered lead, first opportunity, and repeat sourcing. Partner with sales leaders, account executives, and BDRs on partner engagement, lead handoffs, and effective co-selling, including attaching certified, enabled partners for implementation and ongoing Klaviyo management and optimization. Drive the right behaviors with push and pull across content, resources, tasks in the partner portal, and lead registration adoption. Identify high-potential partners through performance and engagement signals, and trigger targeted support when it accelerates results. Fast-track the strongest toward managed status in partnership with the PAM team. Create an exceptional partnership experience at scale Deliver a predictable cadence of digital enablement, partner workshops, office hours, community activities, and demand generation. Ensure partners feel connected and supported, and are enabled to use the right channels and avenues for their needs. Work with Partner Marketing and regional Partner Enablement to build sales plays, enablement cohorts, and demand-gen motions that partners can run with us. Market to our partners, and market through our partners to generate sourced opportunities. Build ecosystem and community along the way. Run the book with data and AI Use partner health data and leading indicators (portal and content engagement, certification progress, lead registrations, pipeline, time to first deal) to decide where monthly GTM motions and sales plays should focus. Catch partners before they go inactive, and re-activate those who have. Surface accounts, opportunities, and untapped revenue or service opportunities for partners, proactively and at scale. Use AI and automation daily to segment the book, personalize outreach, build plays, and clear admin. Who you are You have 5+ years of experience in partnerships, channel, business development, sales, or a related SaaS go-to-market role. You have driven partner-sourced pipeline or revenue through programs and scaled motions, not only through a handful of strategic relationships. You have worked with agencies, consultancies or tech partners that serve small and medium brands, ideally in ecommerce or martech. You have a data-first mindset: you read leading indicators, build segments, and turn them into action in tools like Salesforce and Tableau. You are AI native: you know how to use the content, frameworks, and program resources at your disposal, and you build repeatable workflows, templates, and plays. You communicate well at scale, running webinars, cohorts, office hours, and campaigns that change partner behavior. You are confident working with sales leaders, AEs, and BDRs, and with Partner Marketing, Enablement, and Operations. You have a knack for uncovering revenue opportunities and surfacing them to partners and sales teams. You thrive in a high-pace environment, with a "1% done" mentality: you move fast, ship, learn, and iterate, with no shortcuts in an industry and product that keep innovating. Klaviyo in APAC: We are “1% done” but have big plans for Klaviyo in APAC. Our Sydney team began to take shape throughout 2022 and has now built out our go to market teams in sales, customer success, services, partnerships, marketing, employee experience and product support. We opened our Singapore Hub in late 2025 and are scaling fast. As the team grows we will see a continued expansion of Klaviyo’s customer base and the building of a fantastic working culture in line with what we see elsewhere in Klaviyo but with its own local identity within our Sydney based team. This is your unique opportunity to join us at an early stage and help to shape our future Klaviyo in APAC. One of our values as a company is ‘always learning’ and you can feel that in APAC. People are looking to grow and develop and Klaviyo provides a great platform to do so. As we are still early in our journey in APAC this means there is a lot of headroom to grow and develop within your role - we are looking for the leaders of the future. Proven ability to teach MEDDPICC or an equivalent methodology. A history of recruiting and developing enterprise sellers who self-source pipeline and hit targets consistently. Visit klaviyo.com/careers to see how we empower creators to own their own destiny. Senior Product Manager, Product-Led Growth (PLG) About the Team Klaviyo's Growth team is responsible for making it easier for businesses to discover, adopt, and grow with Klaviyo. We build the product experiences that connect customer value to sustainable business growth, spanning onboarding, activation, self-service purchasing, subscriptions, billing, and monetization. As Klaviyo continues to expand its platform and introduce new products and AI-powered capabilities, our team plays a critical role in helping customers realize value quickly, understand the full breadth of what Klaviyo offers, and seamlessly grow their investment over time. We believe the best growth strategies are built into the product itself. By combining customer empathy, thoughtful design, experimentation, and data-driven decision-making, we create intuitive experiences that drive adoption, conversion, retention, and long-term customer success. About the Role We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to help define and accelerate Klaviyo's product-led growth strategy, with a focus on creating seamless, high-converting customer experiences across the entire product lifecycle. This role sits at the intersection of product experience, growth, and monetization. You'll own key initiatives that help customers move from initial signup to activation, discover and adopt additional capabilities, and expand their relationship with Klaviyo through intuitive self-service experiences. This isn't just about optimizing conversion funnels or running experiments. We're looking for someone who understands that sustainable growth comes from delivering meaningful customer value, removing friction, and building experiences that make it easy for customers to get started, see results, and grow. You'll partner closely with engineering, design, analytics, marketing, finance, and go-to-market teams to identify growth opportunities, shape product strategy, and deliver measurable business impact. You'll have the opportunity to influence how Klaviyo scales its self-service business while supporting an increasingly sophisticated product portfolio and customer base. How You'll Make a Difference Own key product-led growth initiatives across the customer lifecycle, including signup, onboarding, activation, conversion, retention, and expansion, with a focus on improving customer experience and driving measurable business outcomes. Optimize the self-service customer journey by identifying and removing friction across product discovery, account setup, trial experiences, purchasing, and upgrades. Accelerate time to value by building intuitive onboarding and activation experiences that help customers quickly understand Klaviyo's capabilities and achieve meaningful outcomes. Drive conversion and monetization through thoughtful in-product experiences that help customers understand available plans, evaluate additional capabilities, and seamlessly upgrade or expand their usage. Partner on pricing, packaging, and billing experiences to ensure customers can easily understand, purchase, and manage their subscriptions as their businesses grow. Build a culture of experimentation by developing hypotheses, designing and evaluating experiments, and translating insights into product improvements that drive sustainable growth. Define and measure success through clear growth metrics, including activation, trial-to-paid conversion, feature adoption, retention, expansion, and revenue impact. Leverage customer insights and behavioral data to identify opportunities, understand points of friction, and prioritize initiatives with the greatest potential customer and business impact. Collaborate across product and go-to-market teams to connect self-service and sales-assisted growth motions, creating consistent experiences for customers across different segments and stages of maturity. Develop and execute a product roadmap that balances near-term growth opportunities with longer-term investments in scalable, customer-centric product experiences. Who You Are You have 3–5+ years of product management, start-up. consulting, or investment banking experience and have a desire to create and drive growth strategies across the customer lifecycle, including signup, onboarding, activation, conversion, retention, and expansion. You understand the fundamentals of product-led growth and have experience improving meaningful business metrics through product improvements rather than relying solely on marketing or acquisition strategies. You're highly analytical and comfortable defining success metrics, interpreting behavioral data, identifying opportunities, and using experimentation to inform product decisions. You have a strong customer-first mindset and regularly leverage research, feedback, and product usage insights to understand customer needs and inform your roadmap. You understand how product experience and monetization intersect, including the tradeoffs between reducing friction, delivering customer value, and driving revenue growth. You've worked closely with engineering and design teams to ship impactful products, balancing speed, quality, and long-term scalability. You're comfortable operating in ambiguity, can identify opportunities without a predefined playbook, and bring a strong bias for action and execution. You can influence cross-functional stakeholders, communicate a clear product vision, and align teams around measurable outcomes. You think like a builder, with the curiosity, creativity, and ownership mindset to challenge assumptions, experiment with new approaches, and continuously improve the customer experience. Experience with subscription monetization, pricing and packaging, billing, checkout, or self-service upgrade experiences. Familiarity with growth experimentation, funnel analytics, cohort analysis, and tools used to understand customer behavior and product performance. Experience building onboarding, activation, or expansion experiences for complex, multi-product SaaS platforms. Background in martech, ecommerce, CRM, or other data-driven SaaS products. Experience leveraging AI-powered tools and emerging technologies to accelerate product development, experimentation, or customer value delivery. As our platform becomes more powerful and our product portfolio expands, the opportunity to simplify how customers discover, adopt, and grow with Klaviyo has never been greater. Your work will help shape how we acquire, activate, convert, and retain customers while building a more seamless, scalable, and customer-centric growth engine. About the team Klaviyo went public in 2023 and is scaling fast. This is a rare chance to lead and build the Order to Cash (O2C) foundation for a company at this inflection point. The Finance Technology Systems team is part of G&A Systems within Global Technology Solutions (GTS). This group designs, operates, and continually improves the applications and workflows that power how Klaviyo manages money, risk, and financial reporting at scale. The team partners closely with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Treasury, FP&A, Procurement, and Internal Audit, as well as adjacent technology teams like Corporate IT, Data, and GTM Systems, to ensure our back‑office stack is reliable, well‑integrated, compliant, and ready for a public, AI‑forward SaaS business. You will lead Enterprise and International Expansion capabilities that will provide revenue uplift for Klaviyo. Own the O2C track Execute on the roadmap for Klaviyo’s O2C stack aligned to the company priorities by translating business requirements into functional and technical design. Look at O2C systems landscape and provide recommendations to set Klaviyo for the future Ensure we deliver with the highest code quality by thoroughly thinking through test cases and applying rigorous build and test. This isn't a future-state vision, it's work already underway, and you'll own it from a Product standpoint. Design and optimize core Finance processes and systems Have a leader mindset and partner with Controllership, Tax, Treasury leaders to improve and continuously refine end‑to‑end O2C workflows ensuring systems and processes are tightly aligned. We have expanded beyond retail into hospitality, media, healthcare, and business services. Sell to the full buying committee. Get to the CMO, CFO, CIO or CDO. Build champions and test them. Win the competitive deals. Displace the incumbent, hold your price, and have a clear answer on why Klaviyo and why now. Close and forecast with discipline. Run the mutual action plan, security and legal review, and procurement. Forecast against what the customer has agreed to. Grow and renew. Expand into more products and teams, spot risk early, and negotiate renewals that make room for growth. Visit klaviyo.com/careers to see how we empower creators to own their own destiny. Klaviyo's GTM Systems team builds and runs the systems that power marketing, sales, partnerships, customer success, and services. We're looking for a Lenior Technical Project Manager with 8+ years of experience delivering complex SaaS GTM and revenue systems programs, who understands both how the systems work and how the business runs on them, and who is excited to bring AI into how we plan, deliver, and operate. About the team Our GTM Systems team sits at the center of Klaviyo's GTM engine, connecting Salesforce, CPQ, billing and finance systems, customer success and support platforms, and professional services tooling. We own the roadmap that lets our teams move quickly, trust their data, and focus on helping customers grow. As we scale, we're rebuilding parts of that stack around AI and agentic workflows as the operating model, not a bolt-on experiment, and we need a program leader who can deliver that change reliably. About the role As Lead Technical Project Manager, you own delivery of our highest-impact, highest-complexity GTM systems programs from intake through hypercare. Think CPQ replacement, quote-to-cash changes, customer success and support platform upgrades, and AI-enabled workflows that cut across Sales, Customer Success, Services, Finance, and Internal Audit. You turn ambiguous business goals into clear plans, sequence work across many teams shipping into the same core systems, and keep leadership informed with an honest view of commitments, risks, and progress. You'll work hands-on with business systems analysts, developers, architects, vendors, and finance and audit partners, and you'll regularly present to senior and executive leadership. You use AI yourself to run programs faster and better, and you help bring it into the way our teams work. How you'll make an impact Own program delivery end to end: intake, prioritization, scoping, sequencing, status, and operating cadence for a multi-quarter GTM systems roadmap, from discovery through launch and hypercare. Lead cross-functional programs at scale: manage dependencies across Sales, Deal Desk, RevOps, Customer Success, Services, Finance, Legal, Security, and Engineering, including teams that don't report to you. Drive technical decisions with engineers and architects: weigh trade-offs, build-vs-buy calls, integration patterns, and vendor evaluations, and make sure decisions are documented and defensible. Deliver with controls built in: partner with Finance, Internal Audit, and Security on revenue-impacting systems work (SOX/ITGC, access, change management, audit traceability) so controls are designed in, tested, and evidenced. Manage vendors and implementation partners: run joint project plans, steering committees, decision logs, and risk reviews, and hold partners to commitments. Bring AI into GTM and into how we deliver: help scope and ship AI and agentic workflows into production, and use AI tooling to improve planning, status reporting, testing, and documentation. Build the operating model: establish intake, planning, release management, and reporting practices that hold up as the portfolio grows, and mentor teammates on program craft. Communicate with clarity: give GTM Systems, GTM, Finance, and executive leaders a crisp view of scope, timeline, cost, risk, and decisions needed, in the room and in writing. What makes you a great fit 8+ years of technical program or project management, business systems delivery, or GTM/revenue systems experience at a SaaS company, with a track record of owning large, multi-team programs end to end. Deep working knowledge of GTM systems and processes: lead-to-opportunity, quote-to-cash, renewals and amendments, customer success and support, and professional services delivery, and how objects, data, and approvals flow between Salesforce, CPQ, billing/ERP, contracting, and support tools. Experience delivering in a Salesforce-centric environment where multiple teams ship into a shared core system on a common release process. Experience partnering with finance, audit, or compliance functions on revenue-impacting systems and controls. Strong technical fluency: you can read an architecture diagram, discuss integration and data-model trade-offs with developers, and spot delivery risk early. Hands-on curiosity about AI: you use LLM tools in your own work, can talk credibly about where AI and agents help GTM workflows and where they need guardrails, and want to help teams adopt them responsibly. Exceptional stakeholder management and executive communication; comfortable driving outcomes through influence in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience. Nice to haves Experience with CPQ implementations or replacements, quote-to-cash redesign, or billing/ERP integrations (for example NetSuite). Experience with customer success, support, or services platforms (for example Gainsight, Zendesk, Certinia) and contracting tools (for example Ironclad). Familiarity with SOX ITGC, revenue controls, or SOC reporting for vendor-hosted systems. Experience standing up release management or CI/CD for a Salesforce org. Exposure to agentic AI frameworks or MCP-based integrations in a business systems setting. PMP, Salesforce, or similar certifications (or equivalent demonstrated experience). Prior experience at a high-growth software or AI company. Why this role matters at Klaviyo Your programs directly affect how Klaviyo sells, bills, renews, and supports customers, with real visibility to senior GTM, Finance, and executive leadership. You'll lead work that sits at the intersection of GTM systems, finance controls, and AI, a combination that is rare and increasingly valuable. You'll help shape an AI-first delivery and operating model for GTM Systems, setting practices that outlast any single project. Dublin, Ireland (Hybrid: 3 days p/week in-office) Full-time permanent contract About the Team and Role As an Associate Growth Specialist , you are the first human touchpoint for a high volume of inbound demo requests and free Klaviyo accounts . You provide fast, high‑quality first interactions with Klaviyo’s smallest accounts to create a seamless experience from first touch through purchase. This team sits within the Marketing organization as part of the Growth motion and partners closely with Sales, Business Development, Product, and Customer Success. The primary goal of this role is to acquire as many high‑quality new logos as possible while maintaining an exceptional customer experience. You will: Field inbound demand (demos, trials, free accounts, and product inquiries) via phone, email, and other channels. Run consultative, decision‑driven demos focused on one‑call closes whenever possible for smaller opportunities. Do targeted business discovery to understand goals, urgency, and fit. Qualify in or out efficiently , so you know where to double‑down and where to quickly move on. Strategic Finance & Revenue Forecasting Lead About the role Forecasts are only useful if leaders trust them and act on them. We're looking for a data scientist to own revenue forecasting at Klaviyo. You'll build the forecast, and you'll also explain it, defend it, and use it to shape planning and strategy. You'll spend as much time with Finance, GTM, and Product leaders as you do in a notebook. You'll be the person who can say in two minutes what the forecast says, why it moved, and what we should do about it. What you'll do Own the revenue forecast end to end, from building the base model to working with stakeholders to keep it updated with initiatives. Be the voice of the forecast. Brief senior leaders on where we're headed, what's driving it, how confident we are, and what could change the answer. Work closely with GTM, Business Operations, Product Leadership, and FP&A stakeholders to incorporate initiatives into the forecast and build consensus across teams to increase trust. Lead the investigation when actuals diverge from forecast. Quickly determine whether the cause is data, the model, customer behavior, a product or pricing change, or an external event, and tell the business what it means. Define how we measure forecast quality (accuracy, bias, uncertainty) in terms the business understands, and set a standard for how forecasts are reviewed and trusted. Create repeatable RCA frameworks and self-serve outputs and dashboards, so stakeholders can answer routine questions without you. Work with Data Engineering on reliable pipelines and DBT models for forecasting data. Mentor other data scientists, especially on framing problems and communicating results. Build AI skills to refine the model and establish self-serve reporting capabilities that include interpreting performance and autonomous RCA. Who you are You're a clear, concise communicator. You can take a complex analysis and give a CFO or VP the answer in a few sentences, then go deeper when asked. You've done this regularly, not occasionally. You have strong business judgment and a consultant's problem-solving habits. You structure ambiguous problems, form a hypothesis fast, and focus on what matters to the decision. You've influenced senior stakeholders and changed a decision with your analysis, in a fast-moving, high-pressure startup environment where the numbers matter and the timelines are short. You're comfortable being challenged in the room. You have 7+ years of experience across finance, strategy consulting, analytics, or data science, and you're a true hybrid: equally at home discussing SaaS financials (bookings, retention, pricing, how revenue flows through the P&L) and the statistical methods behind a forecast. These are usually two different people. We need both in one, with hands-on forecasting or financial/revenue modeling experience, ideally in B2B SaaS or a subscription business. You're a builder. You're proficient in SQL and Python or R, you've built and shipped forecasts or predictive models, and you know time series fundamentals and how to evaluate a forecast. You don't need to be a specialist in every method. You know when a simple approach is enough and when it isn't. You're also comfortable picking up new skills, such as data engineering, pipeline work, and DBT, to get the job done end to end rather than waiting on someone else. You work quickly and know when "good enough to decide" beats "perfect". You thrive in cross-functional work and enjoy making the people around you better informed. You're AI-first. You already use AI tools such as LLMs and coding assistants as part of how you work: to build and test models faster, analyze data, draft and pressure-test narratives, and automate recurring work. You're excited to explore where AI can make our forecasting more accurate, more explainable, and faster to update (for example time series foundation models, agentic workflows, and AI-assisted analysis), and you bring ideas and examples, not just curiosity. Lead Product Data Scientist, Agents About the Team Klaviyo's Product Data Science team plays a critical role in shaping how we understand, measure, and improve product and business performance. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, and Go-to-Market teams to turn complex data into actionable insights that inform product strategy, customer experience, and long-term growth. As Klaviyo continues to expand its AI-powered capabilities, intelligent agents are becoming central to how businesses engage with their customers. Composer, Klaviyo's AI marketing agent, helps marketers analyze, build, and execute their marketing strategies, while Customer Agent enables brands to engage shoppers and answer questions across channels including chat, email, SMS, and WhatsApp. These products are evolving rapidly, creating new opportunities and challenges in understanding agent performance, measuring customer value, and connecting AI-driven experiences to meaningful business outcomes. Our team takes an AI-first approach to data science, leveraging emerging technologies and agentic tools to accelerate analytical workflows, improve decision-making, and focus our efforts on the complex questions that matter most to customers and the business. About the Role We're looking for a Lead Product Data Scientist, Agents to own and advance Klaviyo's measurement and data science strategy across Composer and Customer Agent, combining deep technical expertise with strong product and business judgment to influence some of our most important AI investments. This is a highly visible, hands-on technical leadership role at the intersection of data science, AI product development, and business strategy. You'll define how we measure the adoption, engagement, quality, cost, and business impact of our AI agents, establishing the analytical foundations that help teams understand what creates meaningful customer value. This isn't just about building dashboards or tracking traditional product metrics. We're looking for someone who can tackle emerging measurement challenges, develop rigorous approaches to evaluating agent performance, and determine whether AI-powered experiences are genuinely improving customer outcomes. You'll combine experimentation, causal inference, and advanced analytics to help leaders make informed decisions in an environment where established measurement frameworks are still evolving. You'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, and executive leadership to shape product strategy, evaluate pricing and monetization opportunities, and translate complex analytical findings into actionable recommendations. You'll also help define the technical direction of agent analytics at Klaviyo, mentor other data scientists, and establish the shared metrics, methodologies, and data foundations that enable teams to make confident, data-driven decisions. How You'll Make a Difference Own agent measurement end to end across Composer and Customer Agent, developing comprehensive measurement frameworks that connect adoption, engagement, agent performance, customer value, and revenue impact. Define what successful agent performance looks like by partnering with Product and Engineering to establish meaningful measures of agent effectiveness, task completion, customer outcomes, failure rates, and the trade-offs between quality, cost, and business value. Build scalable agent evaluation frameworks by combining conversation data, agent traces, tool-call outcomes, human evaluation, and LLM-based classification to assess quality, identify failure patterns, and understand how changes to models and agent behavior influence product performance. Measure causal impact and incremental value through experimentation and advanced statistical methods, including quasi-experimental approaches such as difference-in-differences, matched comparisons, staged rollouts, and synthetic controls, to determine how AI agents influence customer behavior, retention, and revenue. Connect agent performance to business strategy by partnering with Finance and Product teams to evaluate usage-based pricing, packaging, credit economics, model costs, conversion, and the financial implications of product investments. Establish trusted metrics and analytical standards by defining consistent measurement methodologies, governed data models, and evaluation practices that enable teams to make informed decisions as AI products and underlying technologies evolve. Lead with an AI-first approach to analytics , leveraging coding agents, LLMs, and emerging tools to accelerate SQL development, data modeling, dashboard creation, conversation classification, and analytical workflows while maintaining rigorous validation and quality standards. Build scalable, self-service analytics capabilities that empower product managers and cross-functional stakeholders to independently explore agent performance, evaluate customer outcomes, and identify opportunities for improvement. Partner with Engineering and Analytics Engineering to develop reliable instrumentation, data pipelines, and dbt models that capture agent interactions, support robust evaluation, and maintain data quality as new capabilities are introduced. Lead the technical direction of agent analytics , reviewing analytical approaches, mentoring other data scientists, establishing best practices, and raising the bar for statistical rigor, measurement quality, and AI-native ways of working. Influence product and executive decisions by translating complex analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations, aligning cross-functional stakeholders on meaningful metrics, and communicating uncertainty and trade-offs effectively. Shape the future of AI product measurement by continuously evaluating emerging methodologies, challenging existing assumptions, and prioritizing the analytical questions that matter most as Klaviyo's agents and AI strategy evolve. Who You Are You have 10+ years of experience in data science, product analytics, applied statistics, or a related quantitative discipline, including recent hands-on experience measuring AI, machine learning, or LLM-powered products in production. You bring deep expertise in product measurement, experimentation, statistical modeling, and causal inference, with the ability to select and defend rigorous analytical approaches when traditional randomized experiments aren't feasible. You have experience evaluating AI systems in production, including designing evaluation frameworks, analyzing agent interactions or conversations, leveraging human labeling or LLM-as-judge methodologies, and understanding how model, prompt, and tool changes influence product outcomes. You're highly proficient in SQL and Python or R, with experience developing production-quality analytical solutions and familiarity with dbt and modern analytics engineering practices. You take an AI-first approach to your work, actively leveraging coding agents, LLMs, and emerging tools to accelerate analytical workflows while understanding their limitations and ensuring the accuracy and reliability of their outputs. You've demonstrated technical leadership by setting direction on complex analytical initiatives, mentoring other data scientists, reviewing methodologies, and influencing technical standards across teams. You combine statistical rigor with strong product and business intuition, understanding how customer engagement, AI product performance, usage-based pricing, and unit economics translate into meaningful customer and business outcomes. You're comfortable tackling ambiguous, emerging problems where established metrics or methodologies may not yet exist, and can develop practical frameworks that balance analytical rigor with business needs. You have a track record of influencing senior stakeholders, aligning cross-functional teams around shared definitions and priorities, and translating complex findings into clear recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences. You're a compelling communicator who can explain sophisticated analytical concepts, challenge assumptions constructively, and communicate uncertainty and trade-offs with confidence. You thrive in fast-moving product environments, adapt quickly as priorities evolve, and know how to balance analytical depth with the urgency and iteration required to build and improve AI-powered products. You have a degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Finance, Engineering, or another quantitative discipline, or an MBA with a quantitative emphasis. Equivalent hands-on experience in applied data science is equally valued. Nice to Have Experience measuring and optimizing AI agents, conversational AI, or LLM-powered products in a high-growth B2B SaaS or product-focused technology company. Hands-on experience with agent observability and evaluation platforms such as Braintrust, LangSmith, or Arize, including working with agent traces, tool-call data, and evaluation pipelines. Experience with usage-based or consumption-based pricing, credit models, AI infrastructure costs, or LLM unit economics. Experience building governed metrics, semantic layers, metric trees, or standardized measurement frameworks used across multiple product teams. Experience applying classification, clustering, or other advanced analytical methods to large volumes of unstructured text, customer conversations, or agent interactions. Experience developing internal AI agents or AI-powered analytics tools that improve team productivity and decision-making. Familiarity with marketing attribution, incremental measurement, or evaluating the impact of AI-driven customer engagement. Background in marketing technology, ecommerce, CRM, customer-service software, or other data-driven SaaS products. Why This Role Matters AI agents are central to Klaviyo's product strategy and the future of how businesses engage with their customers. As Composer and Customer Agent become increasingly sophisticated, understanding whether these products are delivering meaningful value, how effectively they perform, and where to invest next will be critical to their long-term success. In this role, you'll help establish how Klaviyo measures the effectiveness and business impact of AI agents, developing the frameworks, methodologies, and analytical foundations that inform some of our most important product, pricing, and investment decisions. Your work will directly influence how we improve agent quality, understand customer outcomes, and connect AI innovation to measurable business value. This is an opportunity to combine deep technical ownership with meaningful strategic influence, working alongside a highly collaborative, AI-first data science team to solve emerging measurement challenges and shape how Klaviyo builds, evaluates, and scales its next generation of intelligent products. Here’s a rewrite that uses the structure and tone of the Axon example, adapted for Klaviyo’s senior technical IC role. It makes ownership clearer, keeps the hands-on expectations prominent, and separates candidate qualifications from measures of success. At Klaviyo, we help businesses build stronger relationships with their customers. As our customers grow, our platform needs to support greater data volumes, more demanding workloads, and increasingly complex operations—with the performance and reliability they depend on. Engineering at this scale takes technical depth, sound judgment, and close collaboration. You’ll work across teams to solve challenging problems, turn architectural improvements into production results, and help build a platform ready for our largest customers. Your Impact We are seeking a senior technical leader to own Klaviyo’s approach to enterprise scalability, performance, reliability, and multi-region readiness. Reporting to a VP of Engineering, you will be a senior individual contributor with no direct reports. You will lead through technical expertise, hands-on engineering, and influence, partnering across teams to deliver improvements that matter to our customers. You will identify and remove major bottlenecks, drive platform-wide architectural changes, and establish clear measures of readiness for our largest tenants and most demanding workloads. Your work will span system design, profiling, implementation, and production rollout. You will also help teams adopt practical tools and repeatable patterns that make performance and reliability part of everyday engineering. This role suits an experienced engineer who can move between deep technical investigation and clear executive communication, make and defend architectural decisions, and build alignment across teams. Reports to: VP of Engineering Direct reports: None What You’ll Do Define what scale readiness means. Establish measurable targets for latency, throughput, error rates, and capacity. Build a shared scorecard and align teams on service-level objectives, error budgets, and performance expectations for critical enterprise workloads. Remove the bottlenecks that matter most. Use production data, profiling, and reproducible benchmarks to identify constraints. Partner with service owners to implement fixes and verify improvements under representative workloads. Drive architectural change. Design and implement sharding, partitioning, caching, back-pressure, and workload isolation strategies. Advance multi-region readiness and build safe paths for high-volume data migrations. Make scale engineering repeatable. Create lightweight benchmarks, profiling harnesses, and test environments that teams can use independently. Pair with engineers to turn successful fixes into reusable patterns. Build readiness into delivery. Lead scalability reviews and establish clear, proportionate release gates that surface risks early and help teams ship confidently. Turn incidents into lasting improvements. Lead technical deep dives, identify systemic causes, and work with teams to deliver and validate fixes that reduce recurring incidents. Apply AI where it improves outcomes. Use AI-assisted profiling, workload modeling, synthetic traffic, anomaly detection, and guided runbooks to improve investigation and response. Establish explicit guardrails, evaluate results, and measure operational impact. Connect engineering decisions to customer needs. Communicate priorities, tradeoffs, and results clearly to engineers and executives, tying technical investments to customer experience, enterprise growth, and operating efficiency. What You’ll Bring Deep experience scaling multi-tenant SaaS. You bring 12+ years of relevant engineering experience, with a track record of removing significant bottlenecks and demonstrating measurable production impact. Strong performance and distributed systems expertise. You have hands-on experience with performance engineering, capacity planning, sharding and partitioning, caching, back-pressure, tenant isolation, multi-region architectures, and large-scale migrations. Engineering depth from diagnosis through delivery. You can investigate unfamiliar systems, test hypotheses, write production code, and work with service owners to roll out changes safely. Sound technical judgment. You use evidence to weigh architectural tradeoffs and know when to address an immediate constraint versus invest in a broader platform change. Leadership across organizational boundaries. You align teams around shared outcomes, clarify ownership, and build practical standards that help engineers move faster. Clear communication. You explain complex technical decisions and their business implications to both engineering and executive audiences. Practical AI fluency. You have applied AI tools or automation to engineering work and can evaluate their usefulness, limitations, and operational risks. You are curious about new approaches and disciplined about validating them. What Success Looks Like in 6–12 Months A company-wide scale scorecard is adopted and reviewed regularly, with agreed targets and clear ownership for critical enterprise workloads. Two to three high-impact bottlenecks are removed, with reproducible benchmarks demonstrating sustained improvements. Our largest customer workloads show measurable improvements in tail latency, throughput, and error rates. Multi-region readiness and high-volume migration plans have clear priorities, tested assumptions, and actionable next steps. Teams use shared benchmarks and readiness checks to catch regressions earlier, and repeat P0 incidents decline. AI-assisted tools demonstrate measurable value in investigation or incident response, such as faster regression isolation or fewer noisy alerts, with appropriate controls and observability. About the role Our Customer Success Managers and Renewals Specialists do their best work when the plan, data, and rhythm behind them are solid. This role builds and runs all three. You'll own the numbers and mechanics that tell us who covers which customers, how much capacity we have, and how the book is performing, then turn them into reporting our leaders actually use. You'll sit between CS leadership, Sales Ops, Finance, and Data. Some weeks you'll be modeling territory options before a quarter starts. Other weeks you'll be building the renewal ops view the team checks every morning. If you like work where the answer ships and people use it, you'll like this job. What you'll do Capacity, coverage, and assignments Maintain headcount and capacity models, and keep them current as hiring, attrition, and book growth change the picture. Support account assignment and territory planning for CS leadership: model options, run quarterly rebalancing, and carry out reassignments when someone leaves or a customer's needs change. Keep assignment data clean and consistent across Salesforce, Gainsight, and reporting, so what the field sees matches what leadership sees. Flag where coverage doesn't match customer value or risk, and recommend how to fix it. Business reviews and performance reporting Build and run the data behind weekly, monthly, and quarterly business reviews (QBR/MBR), delivering inputs on time and with a clear point of view. Own renewal ops reporting: upcoming renewals, renewal status and activity, at-risk accounts, and retention outcomes. Forecast and pipeline are owned elsewhere; you'll use the same definitions. Create and maintain CS dashboards and reports that CSMs, managers and LT rely on to run their books. Help drive and maintain rhythm of business reporting across all CS and Renewals segments Analysis and improvement Answer ad hoc questions from leaders with a recommendation, not a spreadsheet dump. Spot patterns in the data (churn drivers, coverage gaps, capacity strain) and bring them to the team before they're asked for. Automate recurring pulls and reports, and document the process so it doesn't live in one person's head. Work with Sales Ops, Finance, and Data teams to make sure definitions and numbers match across the company. Who you are 3-5 years in Customer Success Ops, Sales/Revenue Ops, FP&A, or an analytics role supporting a go-to-market team, ideally at a SaaS company. Strong SQL and comfort in Tableau or a similar BI tool. Salesforce and Gainsight experience Advanced spreadsheet skills. You can build a capacity model that someone else can pick up and trust. Experience with territory design, account assignment, or capacity planning is a big plus. You explain data clearly to people who don't live in it, and you can tell a CSM, a director, and a VP what a number means for them. You're careful with details and still move fast. Reporting that's late or wrong doesn't help anyone. You're curious about why the number moved, not just what it is. You build tools and processes you'd want to inherit, not just ones that get you through this week. Nice to have Experience supporting renewals or retention teams. Familiarity with health scoring or segmentation work. Python or Snowflake experience. This role makes sure that book is run like a business: clear on who we serve and how, deliberate about the experience we create, and measured on what it delivers. This is half strategy, half operator. You'll design customer experiences and programs for our highest-value accounts, and you'll build the operating rhythm, metrics, and processes that keep the high-touch team effective as it grows. You'll work directly with CS leadership, CSMs, Sales, Support, Product, and Marketing, and you'll have room to shape how we serve our biggest customers. What you'll do Shape the high-touch customer experience Design and pilot the moments that matter for high-touch customers: onboarding to value, executive engagement, business reviews, renewal and expansion plays. Define what high-touch should mean: which customers qualify, what they get, and what outcome each touchpoint should create. Turn customer feedback and data into specific changes to programs, playbooks, and engagement models. Work with Product, Support, Marketing, and Sales to close gaps that customers feel across teams. Run the high-touch business Own the operating model for the high-touch segment: coverage, capacity, cost to serve, and how the model changes as the customer base grows. Set the metrics that tell us whether it's working, such as adoption, retention, expansion, and customer sentiment, and build the cadence to review them. Lead the planning cycles for the segment, and make the case for where to invest and where to automate or pool. Build the playbooks, workflows, and tooling the team uses, and keep them current. Lead projects across teams Manage a portfolio of strategic and operational projects from ambiguous idea to launched, measured program. Translate leadership priorities into plans with clear owners, timelines, and success measures. Bring structure to cross-functional problems, flag risks early, and drive adoption of new ways of working. Prepare clear, decision-ready materials for leadership, with a recommendation attached. Who you are 5-8 years in Customer Success, CS Operations, strategy, or program management, ideally in SaaS, with time close to enterprise or high-touch customers. You've designed a customer program or operating model and can show what changed because of it. You think in outcomes first. You can say what problem you're solving, how you'll know it worked, and what you'd stop doing to make room. You're comfortable with data. You can build the analysis yourself in tools like Salesforce, Gainsight, Tableau, or Snowflake, or ask sharp questions of someone who can. You influence without authority, and people across Sales, Support, Product, and CS want you in the room. You write and present clearly, and you can lead with the answer for executives. You like building new things and also making them stick. Experience using AI or automation to scale customer engagement and CSM efficiency Nice to have Experience with customer segmentation, health scoring, or customer journey design. About the Team Klaviyo's Strategic Finance & Analytics team helps leaders understand, measure, and plan for business performance. We work closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Go-to-Market, and Finance partners to turn complex data into financial insight that informs investment decisions, planning, and long-term growth. As Klaviyo expands its platform and launches new AI-powered products, more of our business is becoming consumption-based. That makes it increasingly important to connect what customers do on our platform to what we earn and what it costs us to deliver. About the Role We're looking for a Lead Analyst to build and maintain the models that forecast Klaviyo's recognized revenue and cost of goods sold (COGS). This role blends data science, finance, and data engineering. You'll build scalable, production-quality forecasting systems, and you'll understand the financial mechanics well enough to make them useful for planning. The role starts with a focus on recognized revenue forecasting. From there, you'll build out COGS forecasts, beginning with consumption-aligned infrastructure costs such as message sending and LLM usage, and extending to the rest of our cost base. As more of our products move to consumption models, the systems you build will be the foundation for how we plan, price, and understand margin. You'll report into Strategic Finance & Analytics and partner closely with FP&A, Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Go-to-Market teams. This is a hands-on technical role. You'll own models end to end, set standards for how forecasts are built and evaluated, and help the team grow its capabilities. How You'll Make a Difference Build and maintain forecasting models for recognized revenue and COGS. Start with overall recognized revenue, then extend to consumption-aligned infrastructure costs (message sending and LLM usage first) and, over time, the full COGS base, including cloud infrastructure, SMS and email carrier and vendor costs, AI inference, and support. Connect product workloads to unit economics. Work with Engineering, Product, and Finance to link usage drivers (such as message volume, profile growth, channel mix, and AI feature usage) to both revenue and delivery costs. Build forecasts that scale with the business across multiple time horizons and levels of granularity, designed to extend to new consumption-based products as they launch. Partner with Finance and FP&A to understand planning mechanics and modeling assumptions, and translate them into robust, well-documented frameworks that feed budgeting, rolling forecasts, and long-range planning. Monitor model performance over time , tracking accuracy and bias, detecting drift, and building challenger models to keep forecasts resilient. Lead variance investigations when actuals diverge from forecast, separating data issues, model limitations, customer behavior, pricing or product changes, and external factors. Run scenario and sensitivity analyses to evaluate pricing changes, product launches, vendor and infrastructure decisions, and cost-efficiency initiatives. Partner with Analytics Engineering on reliable pipelines and dbt models that give forecasting a clean, trusted foundation. Establish technical standards for forecasting methodology, evaluation, and code quality. Communicate clearly to technical and non-technical audiences , from Finance and Product partners to executive leadership, through visualizations, narratives, and presentations. Evaluate emerging techniques , including time series foundation models and AI-assisted workflows, where they improve accuracy or speed. Who You Are You have 8+ years of experience in data science, analytics engineering, strategic finance, or a related quantitative field, with hands-on experience building and deploying forecasting models in production. You combine technical depth with finance context. You understand how revenue recognition, usage, pricing, and cost drivers translate into financial outcomes. You have strong foundations in statistics and time series forecasting, and experience applying methods such as hierarchical, probabilistic, or machine learning approaches to business problems. You're highly proficient in SQL and Python or R, with experience building production-quality analytical solutions, and you're familiar with dbt and modern analytics engineering practices. You've worked with cloud data platforms and distributed processing systems. You have experience with revenue, pricing, usage-based, or subscription data, ideally in SaaS or a platform business. You're comfortable with imperfect data definitions, evolving metrics, and tradeoffs between precision and decision usefulness. You can turn ambiguous business questions into well-defined analytical approaches, success metrics, and clear recommendations. You've demonstrated technical leadership by setting direction on complex projects and influencing standards across teams. You're a clear communicator who can explain modeling decisions and tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical audiences, including senior executives. You bring an AI-first mindset and are curious about how LLMs and agentic tools can improve forecasting and analytical workflows. You have a degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Finance, Engineering, or another quantitative field, or an advanced degree with a quantitative emphasis. Equivalent hands-on experience is equally valued. Nice to Have Experience forecasting COGS, cloud or infrastructure costs, or other unit-cost drivers. Experience with consumption-based or usage-based pricing models. Experience supporting FP&A, strategic finance, or investor-facing analysis. Experience building self-service dashboards or forecasting tools used by Finance and Product partners. Experience establishing forecast evaluation frameworks or governance practices. Hands-on exposure to time series foundation models, LLMs, or agentic AI for forecasting and decision support. Why This Role Matters Accurate revenue and COGS forecasts are the foundation for how Klaviyo plans investments, prices new products, and manages margin. As our portfolio adds consumption-based products, the ability to connect customer usage to revenue and delivery cost will become one of the most important inputs to our decisions. In this role, you'll build that capability from the ground up and help make forecasting a trusted, repeatable practice across the company.
